Subject: Post-demo: private deployment latency & peering action items

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we talked through for the private/VPC deployment so your engineers can start prepping. I copied Karthik and Lauren for technical + procurement alignment.

Summary of agreed SLOs / targets (as discussed):
- Inference latency (non-streaming): p50 < 60ms, p95 <= 200ms for the base 7B model under steady state.
- Streaming tail: 95th percentile of end-to-end chunk latency <= 300ms (client -> Redwood edge -> model -> chunks delivered).
- Throughput / concurrency: target 150 req/s sustained with spikes to 300 req/s for short bursts; connection concurrency target ~60 concurrent streams.
- Packet tolerance: packet-loss observed in production should be <0.5% for acceptable quality; jitter budget ~20ms.

Network & topology items we need from OptiMed:
1) Preferred connectivity model: if you choose AWS Transit Gateway peering vs site-to-site VPN, provide preferred route and any Transit Gateway IDs.
2) Egress IPs and NAT configuration (we need stable egress IPs for allowlisting).
3) Network diagram (detailed L3 topology + expected public/private subnets) — helpful to have a diagram for the NOC.
4) MTU and any custom TCP keepalive settings you already enforce.
5) Expected ingress/egress bandwidth during peak test windows.

Proposed load-test window: Sept 22–23 (US/PST mornings). Please confirm availability for a 2-hour run each day so we can validate concurrency and streaming behavior end-to-end.

Attachments: demo-logs-20260914.zip (sample logs we captured), initial SLO proposal (slo-proposal-optimed.pdf).

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Alex: send network diagram and NOC contact (name + email). Target: 9/16 EOD.
- Karthik: define exact perf test plan (tools, synthetic load shapes) and confirm if we need to open TCP ports or change MTU. Owner: Karthik (will reply with checklist).
- Lauren: flag procurement for any early PO/NDA items and confirm DocuSign timeline. Owner: Lauren.
- Rishi: will schedule the NOC call + reserve load-test slots once we have network contacts.

Thanks — want to make the runbook as prescriptive as possible so your infra team can move quickly.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

- Egress: we currently NAT at the TGW; can provide the egress IPs.

I'll loop in our NOC lead (cc'd) — they will send the topology diagram and a preferred contact for Thursday. We can do the first load test on Sept 22 in the 10:00–12:00 PST window. Sept 23 morning is also possible as a fallback.

Thanks Alex / Rishi. Couple technical clarifications from our side before the NOC call:

1) Egress IPs & allowlist: if you NAT at the TGW, can you confirm whether those egress IPs are stable across AZs? We prefer a small set of stable IPs for allowlisting firewall rules — otherwise we'll recommend an IP range + dynamic update.

2) KV cache TTL: for streaming efficiency we'll likely use a per-session KV cache with TTL ~15m during load tests; please confirm your session timeout settings on the client side so we can align.

3) Keepalive / idle timeouts: if there are aggressive idle timeouts in your LB or firewall (<=60s), streaming will break during long LLM responses. Can you confirm any enforced idle timeouts?

4) Test traffic shaping: we'll generate a few traffic shapes — steady 150 req/s, spike to 300 req/s (60s), and sustained streaming-heavy traffic (60 concurrent streams with chunk sizes ~2–4k tokens per minute). If you need different shapes, call it out now.

5) Fallback path: please confirm whether a site-to-site VPN fallback is acceptable if TGW peering isn't ready by Sept 22. The difference in latency is typically +15–40ms.

Lauren — can you take the procurement / compliance follow-up (SOC2 questionnaire + NDA) and own the DocuSign thread? We'll need any PO/contract prerequisites before we run extended soak tests.

Rishi — I'll draft the perf test script and return it here by 9/17 so we can iterate.

-Karthik
